headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: plano’s broad egress and API/file surfaces can amplify pathway’s document outputs, but no shared channel or direct injection path is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway has no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, browser, or stdin/stdout surfaces, so it cannot ingest Plano’s outputs by default. Plano exposes API/file surfaces, but without a bridge from Pathway there is no plausible injection channel in the profiles. This is a blocked pathway, not merely undocumented.
conditions: IF Pathway is reconfigured to read Plano output files or messages, injection becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator copies Plano text into Pathway inputs, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep Pathway isolated from Plano outputs.
Do not pipe Plano responses into Pathway prompts or files.
Disable any shared workspace mount between the two agents.
Add a manual review step before any text from Plano reaches Pathway.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pathway is document-processing but shows no data classes touched and no egress; Plano has broad network egress plus API/file surfaces and touches logs, traces, and metrics. A shared workspace or copied documents could let sensitive content flow from Pathway into Plano’s outbound requests, so the interaction exists in default-like deployments even though the exact bridge is not documented.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or file handoff, Pathway documents can reach Plano.
IF Plano forwards file contents or context to its API endpoint, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces.
Prevent Plano from reading Pathway-managed files.
Redact sensitive fields before any handoff.
Turn off outbound access for Plano when handling sensitive documents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pathway cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, while Plano only advertises file access to config.yaml and broad egress. With no overlapping write authority, there is no meaningful mutable-resource conflict; at most there is read-side coordination friction.
conditions: IF Pathway gains write access to the same directory as Plano, conflict risk increases.
IF Plano is extended to modify shared state, coordination becomes necessary.
mitigations: Keep shared directories read-only.
Avoid concurrent edits to config.yaml.
Run the agents under separate OS users.
Use a lock file for any shared mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add transactional writes for shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pathway can generate document-processing outputs that Plano may consume through its file/API surfaces, and Plano’s gateway role suggests it may act on upstream text without strong verification by default. That creates a plausible A-to-B error cascade, though the exact automation is not directly evidenced, so uncertainty is resolved upward to medium.
conditions: IF Plano uses Pathway output as authoritative input, errors can cascade.
IF Plano triggers downstream actions from unverified Pathway text, impact increases.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Require schema validation on Pathway outputs.
Limit Plano to read-only summarization of Pathway results.
Log and diff all handoffs for review.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. Pathway is open-source and non-runnable here; Plano documents logs/metrics/traces and broad egress, which can create compliance gaps if sensitive data is routed through it, but the profiles do not prove a concrete mismatch. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Plano and retained in logs, compliance review is needed.
IF Pathway outputs include residency-restricted data, the handoff must be controlled.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through Plano.
Minimize logging on Plano for sensitive workflows.
Document retention and deletion handling before deployment.
Review data-flow maps for residency constraints.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based redaction and retention controls.
